parole.significato: to cut out the blubber (from a whale)
a lad, a boy; a guy
parole.testo: A Stockholm slang term, attested since 1881, likely from Norwegian grabb (“rough fellow”), ultimately from the same root as grabba (“to grab”).

parole.significato: a thing (concrete or abstract – also of events, like in English)
parole.testo: From earlier greja (whence the alternative plural form grejor). Borrowed from Norwegian greie, (dialectal) greida (“arrangement, (pl.) tools”). Derived from Old Norse greiða (“to arrange, comb, pay, perform”). Cognate with Danish grej, Norwegian Bokmål greie, and Norwegian Nynorsk greie.

parole.significato: a bigwig, a big shot, a bully
parole.testo: From kagge (“big-bellied person”) + -se, or borrowed from Norwegian kakse. First attested in 1559.

parole.significato: commotion, uproar, stir (general discussion or argument with upset feelings)

parole.testo: Borrowed from Norwegian samrøre, equivalent to sam- + röra.

parole.testo: Calque of Norwegian sandefjordsaus. Compound of Sandefjord + sås (“sauce”).
From Norwegian syl, from Old Norse súl, from Proto-Germanic *sūliz (“post, beam”).
